rv.q: Lombe delivers a tender, cosmic and cleverly unpredictable love story that will leave you wishing for a sequel.

Glorious, tender and profound … In Lynette Linton's glorious two-hander, Tosin Cole and Heather Agyepong make for a terrific pairing … There is great family sadness in both of their backgrounds and its weight on these young people manifests itself in unexpected ways.

This epic new romcom has West End audiences swooning … With fine performances from Tosin Cole and Heather Agyepong, Benedict Lombe’s will-they-won’t-they love story – which has high profile backing from Idris Elba, Little Simz and Maya Jama – is another fresh hit originating from the Bush Theatre … The joy of Benedict Lombe’s...

Time-travel love story with thermonuclear charisma … Benedict Lombe’s multilayered romance benefits from the charm of its two leads at the Duke of York in London … Much excitement has preceded the transfer of Benedict Lombe’s nuanced, beautifully affecting love story from the Bush Theatre — only the third play by a black woman yet to have made...

Benedict Lombe’s drama about two old flames who can’t get over each other is smouldering and soulful … The beginning of Lynette Linton’s production is a deliberate slow burn. The romance between the duo creeps in slowly, but once it lands it tugs on your heartstrings tight.
